transcript.en: Well, you've both been looking at different styles of managing individuals, in companies and the workplace.
transcript.zh: 你们都对公司和工作场所不同风格的个人管理进行了调查，

transcript.en: How's the research going, Philip?
transcript.zh: 飞利浦，你的调查进行的怎么样？

transcript.en: Well, I've been looking at why individualism, I mean individual differences, are such an important area of management studies.
transcript.zh: 我关注于为何个人主义，也就是个体差异是管理研究的重要部分。

transcript.en: When you think about any organization, be it a family business or a multinational company, they are all fundamentally a group of people working together.
transcript.zh: 当你想到任何组织，家族企业或者跨国公司，它们都是一群人在一起工作。

transcript.en: But it's what these individuals contribute to their places of work that makes you realize how important they are.
transcript.zh: 但是这些个人对工作做出的贡献使你认识到他们的重要性。

transcript.en: Of course they bring different ideas,  but it's also their attitudes and their experiences of learning.
transcript.zh: 他们当然带来了不同的观点，但是还带来了他们的态度和学习经验。

transcript.en: Diversity is important in these areas too.
transcript.zh: 在这方面，多样化也很重要。

transcript.en: So why do people behave so differently from one another at work?
transcript.zh: 那么为什么人们在工作中表现的各不一样呢？

transcript.en: There are lots of reasons, but research has shown a lot of it comes down to personality.
transcript.zh: 有很多原因，但是调查显示多数源于性格。

transcript.en: And the other factor is gender.
transcript.zh: 另一个原因是性别。

transcript.en: It's a well-known fact that men and women do lots of things in different ways, and the workplace is no different.
transcript.zh: 众所周知，男人和女人的很多处事方式不同，而在工作场所也一样。

transcript.en: Did you look at the effects of this variation on companies?
transcript.zh: 你注意到这些变化对公司的影响了吗？

transcript.en: Yes, I did.
transcript.zh: 是的。

transcript.en: On the positive side, exposure to such diversity helps encourage creativity which is generally an asset to a company.
transcript.zh: 展现多样性的优点是激发创造性，这对公司来说是一种财产。

transcript.en: But unfortunately individual differences are also the root of conflict between staff and they can lead to difficulties for management, which can sometimes be serious.
transcript.zh: 但是不幸的是，个体差异也是员工冲突的根源，这会导致管理上的困难，有时会产生严重问题。

transcript.en: Thanks, Philip.
transcript.zh: 谢谢，飞利浦。

transcript.en: So now I guess the two main things to remember here are to identify individual talent and then to utilize it.
transcript.zh: 所以我想现在要记住的两件主要事情是辨别个人天赋，然后利用它。

transcript.en: So Janice, you were looking at identifying different talents in workers.
transcript.zh: 那么珍尼丝，你关注于辨别员工的不同才能，

transcript.en: Do you think this is easy for managers to do?
transcript.zh: 你觉得这对管理者来说容易吗？

transcript.en: Well, currently teamwork is in fashion in the workplace and in my opinion the importance of the individual is generally neglected.
transcript.zh: 当前，工作场合流行团队合作，在我来看，个人的重要性普遍被忽视了。

transcript.en: What managers should be targeting is those employees  who can take the lead in a situation and are not afraid to accept the idea of responsibility.
transcript.zh: 管理者应该重视那些主导形势，敢于担当责任的员工。

transcript.en: That's true.Janice.
transcript.zh: 没错。珍尼丝。

transcript.en: But unfortunately many managers think the entire notion of encouraging individuality amongst their staff is far too hard.
transcript.zh: 但是不幸的是许多管理者认为在员工中间鼓励个性是很难的。

transcript.en: Yes.
transcript.zh: 是的。

transcript.en: That may be true but I think one of the most important tasks of managers is to consider the needs of the individual on one hand and group co-operation and conformity on the other.
transcript.zh: 也许是对的，但是我认为其中对管理者最难的事情是考虑个人需求和小组的合作一致。

transcript.en: It requires creative thinking on the part of management to avoid tension.
transcript.zh: 这需要创造性思维的管理，以避免冲突。

transcript.en: So Janice, what kind of people do you think companies should be looking for?
transcript.zh: 那么珍尼丝，你认为公司应该找什么样的人呢？

transcript.en: Well, it has to start from the very beginning when companies are looking for new employees.
transcript.zh: 这得从最初公司开始找新的雇员开始。

transcript.en: When the personnel department is choosing between applicants they need to look for someone who's broken the mould and can think for themselves.
transcript.zh: 当人事部门选择申请人的时候应该考虑那些可以打破常规，自行思考的人。

transcript.en: Instead, people making these decisions often use a range of psychological tests to see if a person is a problem solver, or will do as they're told.
transcript.zh: 相反，人们作决定时通常使用一系列的心理测试，测试这个人是善于解决问题的人还是听话的人。

transcript.en: I'm not convinced these qualities are actually the most important.
transcript.zh: 我不确信这些品质是最重要的。

transcript.en: So do you think being a good team player is overrated?
transcript.zh: 你认为当一名好的团队合作者被高估了？

transcript.en: No, It's not overrated.
transcript.zh: 不，没有高估。

transcript.en: You do need to learn the rules and learn them fast.
transcript.zh: 你需要学习这些规则并且要快速学习。

transcript.en: No individual can get around this if you're working in an organization.
transcript.zh: 如果你在一个机构里面工作，没有人可以逃避这点。

transcript.en: So how should managers deal with this?
transcript.zh: 那么管理者如何处理这种情况？

transcript.en: Rewards. When an individual demonstrates, the behaviour the organisation expects, some kind of incentive can be given.
transcript.zh: 奖励。当个人行为符合组织期望时，应该给予个人某种激励。

transcript.en: What's important here is that this happens right at the beginning, so new recruits learn the rules of the system immediately.
transcript.zh: 重要的是这种情况刚好发生在最初，因此新招募的人员可以迅速领会系统的规章制度。

transcript.en: Also the incentive should be something the individual actually wants, and this isn't always just money.
transcript.zh: 同样激励物也应该是个人真正想要的，而不仅仅总是金钱激励。

transcript.en: To come back to you, Philip.
transcript.zh: 飞利浦，回到你这里。

transcript.en: You were saying that recognition of good performers is essential.
transcript.zh: 你说辨认出好的执行者很重要。

transcript.en: What else should managers be looking for?
transcript.zh: 管理者们还应该找寻什么？

transcript.en: Well, managing people means you not only have an understanding of your employees, but you also recognise the culture of the organization.
transcript.zh: 管理者不仅意味着你要理解你的雇员，你对组织文化也要有认识。

transcript.en: In fact, for some organizations creativity and individuality may be the last thing they want to see during working hours.
transcript.zh: 实际上，对于某些组织来说，在工作期间最不愿意看到的是创造性和个性！

transcript.en: Very true.
transcript.zh: 十分正确。

transcript.en: Yes, but managing people isn't as easy as it looks.
transcript.zh: 是的，管理人不像看起来那么容易。

transcript.en: For example, change in the workplace can be quite tricky, especially if there's a need to increase profit.
transcript.zh: 比如，在工作场所的改革就十分棘手，特别是在需要提高利润的时候。

transcript.en: And at times like these  managers may have to give priority to profit rather than individual staff needs.
transcript.zh: 在这种情况下，经理们可能不得不先考虑利润而不会先考虑个别雇员的需要。

transcript.en: Yes, and that creates difficult situations for people.
transcript.zh: 是的，这会使人们处境困境。

transcript.en: Yes, but what's important is that managers are able to deal with quite high levels of personal stress.
transcript.zh: 是的，但是重要的是经理们要有能力处理高强度的个人压力。

transcript.en: During times of change they should be thinking not only about the strain on their staff but take time out to think of themselves.
transcript.zh: 变革期间，他们不仅要考虑雇员的承受压力，也要考虑他们自己承受的压力。

transcript.en: Absolutely. So what are the implications of that for...
transcript.zh: 没错，那么这么做的影响……
